id: Casey Rocket | As Above, So Down Under: The Return from the Riff Gulag-San Fran, Wellington -Ticket Master
name: Casey Rocket | As Above, So Down Under: The Return from the Riff Gulag
long_description:
Doors Open: 5:30pm

Show Start: 6:30pm




Granted furlough from the gulag, Daft Rocket is crossing the ditch in 2027 and heading to Auckland for the first time with riffs in tow. His first trip Down Under was a sold out scorcher across Sydney, Brisbane, and Melbourne in 2025. Now, The Boy Who Riffed is bringing his frenetic, spellbound optimism to the information chamber of this haunted planet we call home. This month-long trek will span 17 shows across 11 cities throughout Australia and New Zealand - creating a rift in the space time continuum that may take decades to amend. Mostly improvised, rarely sanctified, and remarkably canonized, this mercurial hour of standup comedy is sure to bring families together around a yule log of proficient proletariat rhetoric that neither holds firm a universal truth or chooses to establish a solid foundation as to the nature of words in general. Ultimately: it's riffing, it's good for us, and we're just as happy with a good book - we shudder to consider it any other way.

id: John Craigie | I Swam Here Tour-San Fran, Wellington -Ticket Master
name: John Craigie | I Swam Here Tour
long_description:
Portland, Oregon producer, singer-songwriter and storyteller John Craigie returns to New Zealand in April 2027 on his I Swam Here Tour.
 
Following his first New Zealand shows in 2025, Craigie returns with his latest album, I Swam Here, out now on Zabriskie Point Records. Written and produced by Craigie, the album was recorded between New Orleans and Astoria, Oregon, bringing together the musical spirit of the Gulf Coast with the quieter sounds of the Pacific Northwest.
 
For more than a decade, Craigie has built a devoted following through his warm, sharply observed songwriting and live shows that pair music with humour and storytelling. His touring has taken him across the U.S., Europe and Australia, with appearances at Newport Folk, Pickathon, Edmonton Folk Festival and High Sierra, and performances alongside artists including Gregory Alan Isakov, Sierra Hull, Brett Dennen and Jack Johnson.
 

I Swam Here follows 2024’s Pagan Church, Craigie’s collaboration with TK & The Holy Know-Nothings, which spent six weeks at #1 on the Americana Albums chart. Expansive yet intimate, the new record marks another chapter for Craigie while retaining the sincerity and conversational songwriting that have become central to his work.
 

Craigie returns to San Fran, Wellington on Thursday 15 April and The Tuning Fork, Auckland on Friday 16 April 2027, returning to the same venues that hosted his first New Zealand tour in 2025.
 

San Fran holds a Supervised License. Minors are welcome to attend events at San Fran so long as they are accompanied by a legal guardian at all times whilst at the venue.

id: Inspiral Carpets (UK) The Singles Tour-San Fran, Wellington -Ticket Master
name: Inspiral Carpets (UK) The Singles Tour
long_description:
Madchester royalty return! Inspiral Carpets are part of Manchester's holy trinity with the Stone Roses and Happy Mondays and will bring The Singles Tour to Australia and New Zealand this April and May. 

Back in the early ’90s, when Madchester was at its peak, Inspiral Carpets were perhaps best known for their “cool as fuck” T-shirts, which were essential wear for any young indie fan looking to annoy their parents 

Expect the hits, and nothing but the hits, including This Is How It Feels, Saturn 5, She Comes in the Fall, Joe, Dragging Me Down + More… you will be reminded of just how great they are and how many of their songs you know and love! 

“Inspiral Carpets were perhaps the best singles band of the Madchester era” (Pitchfork) 

Since reuniting, the band has sold out shows across the UK and Europe as well as a bunch of Australian dates on their 2023 tour. Keyboard player Clint Boon says the live show is the strongest it has been “We’re on fire at the moment. We’re playing better than ever, and I think we’re appreciating it more, too… It’s brilliant that we’re still here doing it”. Critics say “This is arguably the best I’ve seen the Inspiral Carpets over the decades… Saturn 5 ends the set, blowing the roof off the venue” (Louder Than War)

Dig out your Cool as Fuck T-shirt that your parents didn’t approve of and get ready for their trademark vocal harmonies and the unmistakable swirl of Clint Boon’s organ… bucket hats welcome.  

moo!
